 Ken Walker (groin) did not practice Wednesday. 
 It’s looking more and more like Walker will miss a second straight game with his groin issue. NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport said Tuesday that he wouldn’t be surprised if Walker sat again in Week 11 against the Cardinals. “He had a sore groin (last week). It’s getting better,” head coach Andy Reid said. “We just don’t want to do something stupid. ... He’s feeling better.” Emmett Johnson, fresh off a monster outing in Week 10, would get another start and profile as a top-5 fantasy option. Johnson will face a Cardinals defense allowing the fifth lowest fantasy points per opportunity to running backs this season. 
 Kenneth Walker 
 KC 
 Running Back 
 #9 
 NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport said he “wouldn’t be surprised” if Kenneth Walker sat in Week 11 to make sure that his groin is fully healed. 
 The crux of this appears to be that Emmett Johnson did so well that there’s no need to rush Walker back to the field. We’ll see how the practice reports trend, but a pop-up groin injury on Friday to a rule-out Saturday never felt like something that assured Walker was playing in Week 11. This will be one to monitor on the practice reports all week, especially with six teams on bye.

 Chiefs declared RB Kenneth Walker (groin), DT Peter Woods, OT Jaylon Moore, QB Garrett Nussmeier, FB Ben VanSumeren, CB Melvin Smith, and RB Jaydn Ott inactive for Week 10 against the Falcons. 
 Walker was ruled out on Saturday, paving the way for rookie Emmett Johnson to potentially see a bell cow role in a plus matchup against the Falcons. Walker should be considered no better than week to week after getting injured in Friday’s practice, but the team has expressed hope that this is nothing more than a one-week injury. We will be monitoring his status all of next week, when the Chiefs begin prepping for Week 11 against the Cardinals.

 Walker sat out Friday’s practice with a tight groin and was officially listed as questionable for Week 10’s game against the Falcons. Now Schultz is reporting the 26-year-old running back has been ruled out. Once that becomes official, Emmett Johnson moves into the low-end RB1 mix in a plus matchup against Atlanta.

 Kenneth Walker (groin) is questionable for Kansas City’s Week 10 game against the Falcons. 
 Not much of a surprise after he sat out Friday with what Andy Reid called a “tight groin.” This has officially waded into “we’ll see” territory over the weekend. Emmett Johnson would be a low-end RB1 with a good workload if Walker is ruled out ahead of Sunday’s games.

 Chiefs coach Andy Reid said Kenneth Walker sat out Friday’s practice with a tight groin. 
 Reid added “we’ll see how he feels through this afternoon, with rehab, and through tomorrow.” Not exactly a glowing endorsement for Walker playing, though we expect the injury report later today to at least read questionable. If Walker were unable to go, Emmett Johnson would probably find himself with a low-end RB1 workload against the Falcons. 
 Kenneth Walker 
 KC 
 Running Back 
 #9 
 Ken Walker had 18 rushes for 102 yards and a touchdown in the Chiefs’ Week 9 win against the Jets, adding four catches for 41 yards and two touchdowns. 
 Walker sliced through a low-energy Jets defense time and again in the first half. He was more involved than usual in the pass game, taking over as KC’s primary pass catcher out of the backfield after Emmett Johnson’s big PPR performance in Week 8 against Denver. Walker would have likely had a bigger day if the Chiefs hadn’t benched their starters in the fourth quarter, up my multiple scores. This was Walker’s third multi-touchdown performance of the 2026 season, and it marks the fourth time this season he’s had at least four receptions in a game. Walker will remain a high-end fantasy play in Week 10 against the Falcons. 
 Kenneth Walker 
 KC 
 Running Back 
 #9 
 Kenneth Walker rushed 21 times for 69 yards in the Chiefs’ Week 8 loss to the Broncos, adding four catches for 15 yards. 
 Emmett Johnson stole the show today with 128 yards and a touchdown on five receptions. Johnson blew by the Broncos’ defense for a 73-yard touchdown, which alone would have been enough for a breakout performance. The good news for Walker drafters is that Johnson only carried the ball once. Walker also matched him in targets at five apiece. Walker is now coming off his two worst rushing performances of the year in tandem with the Chiefs’ first two losses. It’s safe to assume the two are related. With a down-bad Jets defense on deck, we fully expected Walker to get back on track as a top-end RB1 in Week 9. 
 Kenneth Walker 
 KC 
 Running Back 
 #9 
 Kenneth Walker rushed 14 times for 36 yards in the Chiefs’ Week 7 loss to the Seahawks, adding 21 yards on four receptions. 
 Walker was held to below 4.9 yards per carry for only the second time this season while also failing to find the end zone for the second time through six games, with his longest rush going for a meager seven yards. Seattle had all the answers on the defensive side of the ball as they held the Chiefs to just 213 yards of total offense. One of fantasy’s breakout stars in the early going of the 2026 season will face another difficult matchup on the road against the Broncos in Week 8, where he remains an elite RB1. 
 Kenneth Walker 
 KC 
 Running Back 
 #9 
 Ken Walker had 19 rushes for 128 yards and two touchdowns in the Chiefs’ Week 6 win against the Chargers, adding two catches for 11 yards. 
 The Chiefs once again leaned hard on the rushing attack, running the ball 24 times while attempting 30 passes on the day. Walker breezed through a lifeless LA defense from start to finish. On many of his carries Walker was not touched until he was five or six yards beyond the line of scrimmage. Walker, who accounted for 19 of the team’s 24 rushing attempts, is perhaps the most important player in fantasy football through Week 6. He’ll be an RB1 in Week 7 against his former mates in Seattle.
